top.title: METR finds Anthropic may have crossed its own AI acceleration warning threshold back in July
top.snippet:
Nonprofit METR spent eleven weeks auditing Anthropic's internal research data and concluded that the pace of model development has roughly doubled, with about 80 percent of the speedup driven by AI-assisted research. Anthropic redacted the most informative evidence, though, which means the public has to rely on METR's judgment "much more than would be ideal." There are also skeptical voices inside the company.

top.aiSummary: METR found Anthropic’s model development roughly doubled in speed, with AI-assisted research driving about 80% of the acceleration.

Gerald Charles opens first shop-in-shop in Taiwan
Swiss watch brand Gerald Charles has opened its first shop-in-shop in Taiwan, located within Chung Mei Watch’s Nanjing store in Taipei, just ten months after entering the market.

oneSentenceSummary: TikTok and Walmart are taking charge of the shop window. Jewellers are becoming guests in someone else's store.
editorialTake:
I think luxury brands should treat platform checkout as a margin decision before treating it as a growth opportunity. The risk is paying for access without earning a customer relationship.

TikTok’s standalone Shop app offers exclusive deals and checkout, while Walmart’s Sparky is adding visual recognition and cart generation. Both put more of the purchase inside a retailer’s interface. Palace’s in-store-only Burberry capsule offers an alternative, but exclusivity alone does not establish how a brand earns visibility inside a shopping app.

Next quarter, I would test one jewellery collection through a platform and measure contribution after fees and returns. Keep an exclusive assortment on owned channels to compare repeat purchases against the same period’s platform buyers, rather than judging the trial on gross sales.
